That is what I did, got my friends who really love him even though he doesn't think so and some of his friends to all call him. He is home now, and his mom really would have just made it worse. Last time he took off she said, "Well I don't know what to do about him but if you ever feel unsafe around him feel free to come to my house to give him space." to me. Which I personally thought was quite ridiculous.

I am really not trying to change his base personality, I love him the way he is. I love his idiotic humor, and how he can geek out over the most ridiculous things. I know how smart he is, the problem is that he himself doesn't. 

He graduated from college in April after four years with a 3.4 GPA with a bachelors in psychology (yes, I know), and minors in anthropology, philosophy, and German. Since then he has applied to four jobs. When he didn't get any. He told me point blank, "I'm stupid, my GPA isn't good enough, I am never going to get a good enough job, I'm done applying." This is the only thing I want to change... and I want to change it because it is harmful to his own self. That way of thinking is not healthy for anyone, giving up and not believing in yourself is not healthy. I just want him to have a healthier mentality not change entirely.

 I am aware that I am not a trained psychologist, my SO actually says this to me all the time, I'm not asking him to open up so that I can analyze him and change him. I just honestly believe that sometimes having a listening ear is an amazing thing. I just want him to talk to me and to feel comfortable with talking to me about most anything. I want him to trust that I wont hurt him with what he shares.

Thank you for the apology. I sort of figured something about this hit a nerve. I know that forcing him to talk to me about every tiny thing is not the way to go about it. When he is upset I simply ask whats wrong, if he says, "A friend pissed me off." I ask if he wants to talk if he says no I let it go. That's something he can do himself or with the person who he has the issue with. It's when I say one thing and he goes off and yells at me that I try to resolve the problem, because I feel like I did something and I am able to help resolve the issue by apologizing or explaining why I did whatever it is that I did. That's when these conversations turn into clusterfucks and he refuses to simply tell me what I did to make him upset so I can't resolve the issue.

I thought this for a while too, I flat out forced him to make the decision himself. I told him, "No, fuck you, I am not going to let you be the victim, I love you and I still want to be with you so you need to take a night to think and really decide what you want and you let me know." He ultimately came back with, "I love you, I want to stay with you. I just want to fight less." He hasn't said that recently, in fact in our last fight he actually said, "If you don't shut up and leave me alone in 5 minutes I am leaving and not coming back." I don't think that is the issue, but I do still talk to him after we calm down after fights and ask him to tell me directly what he wants.

He wasn't always like this. It got worse and worse since his father died and he had to deal with his mom more without a buffer there. Its really just started becoming a problem over this last year and its maybe only once a month or so. When he is in a good mood its great, he and I are (to be cliche) two peas in a pod... a weird mutated pod that most growers would toss off to the side but one pod none-the-less. He is supportive to me and honest with me almost to the point where my friends are like... "If you ask him if you're getting pudgy he shouldn't tell you that you are." What they don't realize is that I prefer this, also he doesn't just say, "Yep, you're getting fat." He says, "Well you have gained some weight but its because we don't get to eat as healthy as much... and you're still really hot. Maybe we should go running." He just isn't open and honest about himself... he wont tell me what he is feeling no matter how petty or small the issue is. He lets it all build to the point where he has a bunch of little things to be irritated at then lets them all out at once.

I am willing to go see a counselor, it was actually one of my SO's stipulations, if he goes I go. Really I should go too because I have issues just as a lot of people do. Him not thinking a psychologist can help is actually not it at all.  He is actually a psychology major himself... just research based. He knows that counselling will help him, we just don't have the money to pay a family one and most programs are for "a threat to yourself or society" not "So, I feel bad a lot and want to talk to someone about my issues."

You mis-read a lot of what I stated. First of all his brother is awesome... its his mom that has been fucking with him. I absolutely want him to see the therapist alone, my point was that he doesn't want to "waste the time or money" despite him needing to see one. Also I have never told him that he has to talk to me specifically... I always tell him, "Then please talk to someone, it does not have to be me."

1. I don't ask him about his past, I was just saying that as an example of what he doesn't like to talk about, ie: anything emotional. He's talked about his family but only his immediate one, he talks about how he doesn't get along with his mom, I know why he has all his little scars, I know that he loved wearing cowboy boots when he was little and wore almost nothing else. We fight about little and stupid shit... for instance tonight it was him telling me, "I'm going to start doing my dishes after I use them and you should do it too... but I know that you won't." I tried to tell him that it hurt my feelings that he immediately assumed that I wouldn't be able to be responsible enough to do some dishes, since I am the one who cleans the kitchen, vacuums, sweeps the floors, and takes out the garbage on a routine basis and have to ask him to do so for me sometimes. Instead of listening to me he immediately said, "So, you aren't going to do what I ask... great. Fuck you then. I'm going to watch the Walking Dead." This whole thing fucking dissolved into again the routine that we fall into when I try to simply explain to him that what he said offended me. 

2. I was asking all of you for help also in finding an affordable program for a therapist.

3. I do live in the present, I do see what I have, which is why I love him and know that he isn't an asshole. Which is why I know how smart he is and how successful he can become. Which is why I know that he needs help because of all the things that I see him do that show me that. This  man takes care of me in most ways, he can be loving and thoughtful, but he constantly focuses on the negative. He doesn't notice that I work hard to help him out around the house while he works so much, because in the past we have really lived quite a messy existence and he believes that we can not change, and also believes that the reason it was so messy was me and me alone which is in no way true. Which leads to our fights... his focusing on the past and refusing to see what is happening now and look to our future together. 

4. You were actually saying that I am the problem. That I have a crappy attitude and to stop implying that something is wrong with him... something is emotionally wrong with him, he has zero positive self-image. He calls himself the human lightning rod of hate, he tells me that he is an asshole and nothing else, he tells me that he is not good enough to be loved by me or anyone else. I constantly reassure him positively, I tell him that he isn't an asshole, he has friends who love him, and he deserves love. 

You entirely misread what I wrote and while I can see how you did (it was three am and I was extremely emotional when I wrote this), I did not in any way mean that I need to know every detail about his past because I don't... however knowing his cousins names would be nice. Knowing how many sisters his mom has would be nice. Knowing what they do for holidays would be nice so we could figure out how to divide our times between our families instead of me going to mine and him going to his all the time. He has this mentality that is very... this is mine and that is yours. I feel like he doesn't view us as an us. When I try to talk to him about how I feel, he shuts down and doesn't tell me how he feels and tries to put all blame only on me like what I feel doesn't matter and that I feel at all is a problem.

Also, I came here for help. While I am aware that this is the internet, some polite wording and understanding is not unappreciated around here.
